reviews.body: Thanks for updating the defaults and including the saved-config note. The live checks surfaced a couple of compatibility issues with MCP tools and explicit token limits, detailed inline. I’d like us to address those before merging. The migration example would also be helpful, though I wouldn’t hold up the change for that alone.

review_comments.body: I’m seeing a compatibility issue with MCP tools here: Luna returns HTTP 400 for function tools with reasoning_effort="medium" through Chat Completions. The same exchange works with GPT-5, and with Luna when reasoning is disabled. Would it make sense to revisit the interim configuration in #1129 so these aliases keep working with tools while Responses support is pending?

There’s another compatibility detail with openai-text: calls that set max_tokens worked with GPT-4.1, but Luna rejects that parameter and asks for max_completion_tokens, even with reasoning disabled. It looks like DD forwards it unchanged. Translating the limit for the affected OpenAI models, with a test for an explicit token limit, would help preserve those calls.

A small YAML example might make this migration easier. If someone changes only the model name, the saved temperature and top_p values remain, but reasoning_effort="none" is missing, which returned HTTP 400 in my check. Showing the inference parameters alongside the model would help users update without resetting their custom configs.

No actionable new issues were found. Live OpenAI behavior was not tested. I have read the DCO document and I hereby sign the DCO.

Thanks for the live checks. Pushed a commit on top:
- `max_tokens` is now sent as `max_completion_tokens` on `api.openai.com` endpoints (other OpenAI-compatible servers keep `max_tokens`; an explicit `max_completion_tokens` in `extra_body` wins), with sync/async tests for an explicit token limit.
- Added a YAML example to default-model-settings.mdx showing the inference parameters (incl. `reasoning_effort`) next to the model.
- Not changed yet: the HTTP 400 for function tools with `reasoning_effort="medium"` on Luna via Chat Completions. Going by your check that Luna works with tools when reasoning is disabled, I'd suggest `reasoning_effort: none` on `openai-reasoning`/`openai-vision` as the interim until Responses support (#1033), with a docs note that those aliases don't use reasoning for now. The catch is that `openai-reasoning` stops reasoning, which is why I'm asking first: if that works for you, I'll push it, and the live tool-call check would still need someone with an OpenAI key.

This reply was drafted with the help of an AI assistant (Claude Code) and the changes were not run against the live OpenAI API.
